mechanism.deepestCause: corpus readiness is not an input to composition: compose() at company-intelligence-lab.html:991 passes window.RLDATA into INTEL.runAdapters (rlcompanyintel.js:1198) and INTEL.buildCoverageAccount (rlcompanyintel.js:1243), neither of which receives a readiness argument, so an empty cache and a company with no source are the same observation
mechanism.orderingIsUnconditional: paintFromEmbedded() calls run() synchronously at company-intelligence-lab.html:1707 and boot() reaches its first loadCorpus() only at company-intelligence-lab.html:1749, so the first composed paint of every load precedes the first corpus request by construction, not by a race
mechanism.claimIsUnconditionalProse: company-intelligence-lab.html:1460-1462 emits the coverage sentence with no branch on readiness
mechanism.runStatusIgnoresReadiness: company-intelligence-lab.html:1484 passes composed unconditionally; setBodyState at company-intelligence-lab.html:787-791 writes data-run-status from its parameter and data-corpus-status from module scope with no consistency rule between them
mechanism.facet2Ordering: applySubject() composes and renders at company-intelligence-lab.html:1503-1504, then calls loadCorpus() at :1507, and the corpusStatus reset lives inside loadCorpus() at :1540 — one turn after the paint has already copied the old value

historicalKnownLimitationAtScope1.statement: The defect and its cause are both established. What is established: at dc54a8547, the first composed paint of every load precedes the first corpus request unconditionally, so data-run-status reads composed while data-corpus-status reads pending; in that window, with ZERO injected delay on a cold cache, the cockpit prints '15 of 15 mandatory dimensions have no usable source in this run' and all four horizon cards read none/absent, against a settled 13 of 15 in which three horizons carry directions; a case-insensitive body-text scan for readiness wording returns nothing; the magnitude falls to 14 of 15 on a warm cache because loadOne serves one bar leg synchronously, so a returning reader sees a smaller but still wrong overstatement; and during a manual apply data-corpus-status retains the previous subject's value, observed reading loaded for a subject whose corpus had not been requested. What is NOT established: a printed count that drifts behind that stale attribute, which is reachable by construction but was not produced because both subjects tried settle at the count they showed; behaviour under file://, where the corpus resolves to unavailable rather than staying pending; the window's width on a real network; and which of the three remedies in design.md is correct. Scope 1 has since closed the last of those observations: as of 2026-08-23 the corpusStatus reset precedes the paint in applySubject(), so during a manual apply data-corpus-status reads pending for the subject on screen rather than retaining the previous subject's value. Every other statement here still describes live behaviour, because facet 1 is untouched.
